title: Separate framework engineering state from adopter project state for V0.1 forks

spec.unmetRequirement: The fork or clone is the V0.1 distribution mechanism, but the repository conflated Golden Path's own framework-development workload with the adopter's project. All canonical state lived in one flat engineering/ directory, tests required every artifact to derive the framework workload, instructions directed agents to that workload as the project, the local edit capability was scoped to framework work, and every executable file needed an individual path binding. A fork could not record the adopter's own intent without failing checks or blurring framework and adopter ownership, authority and provenance.
spec.simplestViableOption: Keep engineering/ as framework state and add an optional flat project/ directory for adopter state using the same schema and invariants. Derive ownership from location. For V0.1, reject authoritative graph references across the boundary, reject framework-specific agent and skill kinds in project/, and let project implementations bind a directory under the existing single-owner rules. Widen local edit scope to adopter project state and implementation within the human-authorized task.
spec.selectedOption: Adopt that option. Amends adr-bootstrap-minimum's single flat engineering directory to two flat directories distinguished by owner, still with no manifest, aggregate ledger, project ID or tenancy. IDs remain globally unique. Missing project/ means no adopter outcome is established yet. The cross-boundary rule is a V0.1 isolation rule that prevents framework approvals, policies, evaluations and provenance from satisfying project authority or traceability; it is not a permanent claim that framework and project state can never be related, and typed conformance or governance relationships may be earned later. Rejecting project agent and skill artifacts prevents framework engineering-environment semantics from leaking into adopter state; how agents that participate in engineering and agents inside the engineered system should be represented remains an explicit open question. Directory binding is a plain directory path with a trailing slash, not a pattern language. Upstream framework approvals stay unchanged as framework provenance.
spec.capabilityGained: A fork can persist and validate one or more adopter workloads and their implementation boundaries with unchanged traceability and invariant enforcement, while the validator structurally prevents framework approval, policy or evaluation from authorizing adopter state.
alternatives: Allow additional workloads in engineering/: rejected. Nothing would identify framework versus adopter ownership, adopter artifacts could attach to framework decisions or policies, IDs would share one directory, and a fresh agent could not distinguish no project from the framework as the project.
Add a domain field to every artifact: rejected. It requires a schema change and duplicates what the owning location already expresses.
ID prefix convention: rejected as fragile and not a meaningful ownership boundary.
Rename engineering/ to framework/: deferred. Clearer, but broad churn for V0.1; the meaning is documented instead.
Package, installer, template generator or synchronization mechanism: not earned; the fork itself is the V0.1 distribution mechanism.
Keep file-by-file implementation binding for adopters: rejected. It conflicts with req-traceability and makes real adopter repositories impractical.
Glob patterns or a generalized ownership engine: not earned; one plain directory binding per path is sufficient.
spec.simplerOptionAssessment: Existing traceability already confines evaluations and approvals to their derived workload, but nothing marked ownership, so a project artifact could reference framework decisions or policies. The location boundary plus one cross-boundary reference rule is the smallest mechanism that makes both statements true: framework state governs the environment and project state governs the system being built. No new artifact kind, schema field or directory structure beyond project/ is required.
spec.operationalResponsibility: Golden Path maintainers own the boundary rule, directory-binding semantics, loader behavior and their regressions. Adopters own everything in project/, including their own approvals and policies. Forkers who change framework state in their fork remain subject to the same transition checks and need their own decisions. Upstream synchronization, framework upgrades in forks, tamper detection, CODEOWNERS and project-owned agent or skill artifacts remain deferred.
spec.rationale: Release-readiness review for V0.1 found that a fork could not represent an adopter's own workload without violating repository tests. The owner classified this as release-blocking and required that framework provenance must not become adopter authority. The existing cap-edit scope, approved local bootstrap simplification and related contracts/tests/documentation, did not cover adopter state or implementation; this decision governs that same-classification scope change. Upstream approval records in earlier decisions describe framework decisions by the upstream repository owner at their dates; they are preserved verbatim and do not approve adopter project decisions.

authorityChanges.reason: Local edit scope adds adopter project/ state and adopter implementation files within the human-authorized task to the existing framework scope, which is unchanged. External services, deployment, push, merge and publishing remain excluded.

approval.reviewer: Upstream Golden Path repository owner, in the Copilot conversation
approval.source: Explicit approval in the upstream owner's Copilot conversation on 2026-09-23; the statement and scope are preserved here. No hosted review URL or authenticated reviewer identity is asserted.
approval.statement: Approved, with the following refinements. The framework/adopter boundary is earned by the fork/clone usage requirement, and the optional project/ directory is an appropriately small V0.1 physical representation.
approval.scope: engineering/ remains framework state; optional adopter-owned project/ with missing meaning no known adopter outcome; no cross-boundary authoritative graph edges as a V0.1 isolation rule; project agent and skill kinds rejected as a documented model limitation; simple directory binding for project implementations; cap-edit local scope covering adopter project state and implementation within the human-authorized task, excluding external services, deployment, push, merge and other external effects. Excludes renaming, manifests, project IDs, tenancy, packaging, installers, synchronization, CODEOWNERS and runtime-agent representation.
